$doc: Shape of every fixture in this folder (dashboard-schema §26 'Presentation keeping'). Agent 1's state machine consumes these; scripts/verify-presentation-fixtures.mjs and tests/presentation-keeping.test.ts run them. This file is documentation - the runner skips it.

contract.api: step(state: KeeperState, event: KeeperEvent, config: KeeperConfig) -> { state, actions: PresentationAction[] }; initialKeeperState(); keeperConfig({keepPresentation, onEnd}); run(events, config)

fixtureMapping.input: -> user-input (the machine attributes a drop to the human by proximity - USER_INPUT_MS - not by a cause field)
fixtureMapping.presentation.cause: documentation for the reader; the machine infers it (dropped when adapting)
fixtureMapping.intermission{active}: -> ad-break{active} (the controller's veil boundary is a boundary)
fixtureMapping.action.t: = the at of the event that produced it; action.facet = the fixture facet id

contract.adapter: scripts/verify-presentation-fixtures.mjs viaStep() and tests/presentation-keeping.test.ts do this mapping; the machine itself is never edited to fit a fixture
contract.machineConstants: USER_INPUT_MS = 1000 (fixtures use options.inputWindowMs 1500 only for the runner's own I3 attribution; every fixture input->drop gap is <= 200 ms so both agree); CORRELATION_MS = 1500

fixture.name: kebab-case id, unique

options.inputWindowMs: how long after a human input a drop of unknown cause is attributed to the human (default 1500)

fixture.events: array of {t, kind, ...} sorted by t ascending (ms from fixture start)

expect.actions: array of {t, action, facet} the keeper must emit, in order - EXACT: nothing more, nothing less

fixture.contestable: optional true - the verifier's reading of an ambiguous spec sentence; Agent 1 may propose a change in review with the sentence cited

presentation.note: the player's presentation state changed. cause=user when the adapter saw a human control fire; site when it correlates with the site's own boundary; unknown when the adapter cannot tell - the keeper then attributes it by the input window (a recent `input` => user) or a live/just-ended ad or ended signal (=> site)

input.note: a genuine human input reached the page (the host forwards keys; the bootstrap posts pointerdown as 'interaction')

ad-break.note: the adapter's frame.adBreak signal, raw (cover-slow debounce is the intermission controller's job, not the keeper's)

intermission.note: the intermission controller's veil state; active:false is a boundary even when no ad-break:false arrived (the §26 safety timeout)

playing.note: content playback resumed (after an ad, after a restart)

tick.note: time passes; nothing else. Lets a fixture assert that NOTHING happens for a while

actions.enterFullscreen: re-invoke the player's own fullscreen control (adapter-named presentation action)
actions.enterTheater: re-invoke the player's own theater control

invariants.I1-no-action-during-ad: no action may be emitted while an ad-break/intermission is active (restoration happens at the boundary the site created; presentation keeping never alters an ad)
invariants.I2-standing-instruction-only: an enter* action requires facet.keepPresentation === true; a play action requires facet.onEnd !== 'none'. Any action without its standing instruction FAILS the fixture regardless of `expect` - this is the synthetic-interaction ban
invariants.I3-user-exit-never-fought: after a user-caused drop (cause user, or unknown within inputWindowMs of an input), no enter* action until the human re-enters the state (a presentation event with cause user and state != none)
invariants.I4-restore-the-state-the-human-had: the action restores the state last established by the human (fullscreen -> enterFullscreen, theater -> enterTheater), never a different one
